title: Opposite — only means are effects; not attainment of beatitude (Durandus)
source_text: VIII. Alii vero contra pretendunt sola media ad aeternam beatitudinem esse effectus praedestinationis, minime autem ipsam beatitudinis assecutionem. Et hoc quia nomen praedestinationis restringunt ad decretum de gratia communicanda, nec eo comprehendi volunt decretum de danda gloria. Quae est opinio Durandi, teste eodem Gregorio de Valentia loco modo citato.
pass_a_gloss: But others on the contrary maintain that only the means to eternal beatitude are effects of predestination, but by no means the very attainment of beatitude. And this because they restrict the name of predestination to the decree of communicating grace, and will not have the decree of giving glory comprehended in it. Which is the opinion of Durandus, the same Gregory of Valencia bearing witness in the place just cited.
pass_b_english: Opposite camp: only means-to-beatitude are effects.
Attainment of beatitude itself is not an effect.
Because praedestinatio = grace-decree only — Durandus (via Valencia).
